conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Point Cloud Scan (LiDAR)
style.description: A LiDAR scan made only of measured dots on near-black: a scanner head on a tripod turns while a thin bright laser fan sweeps the room and the world appears dot by dot, coloured by range (cyan near, yellow, magenta far) and shaded by return intensity. No surfaces are ever drawn: objects (a figure, a chair, a bicycle, a plant, a table, walls with a door and a window) exist only as ray targets. The scan shows the tells of a real terrestrial scan: rings and lines that spread with distance, and scan shadows — empty holes behind every object that the laser could not see, hidden from the scanner's own viewpoint and dramatic once the camera orbits away. A second scan from another tripod fills the holes.
motion: A dot exists only once the laser has reached its column: reveal time = sweep start + column / columns x sweep duration.
The head yaws with the sweep; a thin bright fan joins the laser origin to the current column's hits.
Fresh dots flash white for ~0.2 s and settle to their range colour (cyan near -> yellow -> magenta far).
Camera: hold still while dots appear; one move per beat (into the scanner's own eye, then out and above to show the scan shadows).
A second tripod scans from elsewhere and its dots fill the shadows of the first.

notes.mechanism: scan.js: rays cast analytically (floor, walls with door/window holes, boxes, cylinders, spheres, capsules) from each tripod in vertical columns; a dot's reveal time = sweep start + column/nAz x dur; dots sorted by reveal so drawRange = dots measured by t.
notes.counter: the on-screen counter shows the real number of dots drawn at that frame
